title: Stop a spinning raw egg and it starts again
pause_note: v20, Kitchen Science, hook=why len=short look=flat. WHY hook at 0 s: frame 0 = a raw egg on a wooden board turning again right after a finger lifted off it (motion arcs, finger just above it); 0.4 s finger presses, egg stops, ~2.0 s finger lifts, ~2.5 s egg creeps round again (hold 0.8 s = clean restart). Wrong guess (a sloppy stop) killed at ~4 s by a boiled egg stopped the same way that stays still. Reveal at ~7.8 s on 'Look inside': the raw egg's shell is cut open in place (fills >= 60 % of frame), the white and yolk are still swirling while the shell is pinned. Explain inside the cutaway: swirl drags the shell round on 'drags'. Boiled cutaway is solid and stops all at once. End: 'Raw?' over the restarting raw egg = frame 0 (loop). Related: ep 23 (spinning coin). No mascot.

beats: Why won't this egg stay stopped?
It's not a sloppy stop. A boiled egg, stopped the same way, stays still.
Look inside. Your finger only stopped the shell.
The runny inside keeps swirling, and when you let go, it drags the shell back around.
A boiled egg is solid, so it all stops at once.
